simple.meaning: צָלַל (tsâlal) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to shade , as twilight or an opaque object.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Nehemiah, Ezekiel, beginning at Nehemiah 13:19. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to צָלַל (H6751) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: צָלַל (tsâlal) / H6751 is traced through Nehemiah 13:19, Ezekiel 31:3 with source-language evidence and verse context.

structuredEvidence.definition: to shade , as twilight or an opaque object

firstOccurrence.englishText: It came to pass that when the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the Sabbath, I commanded that the doors should be shut, and commanded that they should not be opened until after the Sabbath. I set some of my servants over the gates, so that no burden should be brought in on the Sabbath day.

Hiph`il Participle מֵצַל חֹרֶשׁ Ezek 31:3 a shadowing wood (but strike out ᵐ5 . Co Toy Krae).
